subject: Brendan was shocked to be told he'd had a heart attack
posts:
A tiny wrist scratch hides a life-threatening reality. Victoria's cardiac rehab programs slash death risks by 75%, yet 80% of patients skip them.
Evidence: Rehab saves lives, Patients skip care, Systemic recovery
#Aletheia #Health

Hospitals claim a simple six-week cardiac rehab program of exercise and counseling dramatically slashes the risk of a second heart attack and death by 75%.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The program is incredibly effective, but 80% of patients skip it. Minimally invasive stents make patients feel instantly cured, leading them to ignore lifelong recovery.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.8, +0.8) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — Awakening into Grace.
While systemic communication gaps leave patients overwhelmed at discharge, the clinical data is undeniable: rehab actively saves lives for those who walk through the door.

A Monash University study of 7,100 Victorian patients found only 20% attend cardiac rehab. Shorter hospital stays and quick-healing radial artery stents trick patients into thinking they are fully recovered.

The Poison:
Modern medical miracles are a double-edged sword. By making heart procedures feel as minor as a scratch, we accidentally desensitize patients to the chronic, lifelong nature of cardiovascular disease.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a Logical error (HOW). The physical fix of a stent is confused with the systemic cure of lifestyle change. Patients mistake a patched artery for a healed heart, skipping vital rehab.

Social Physics Analysis:
Human psychology naturally seeks the path of least resistance. When high-tech interventions minimize physical trauma, they inadvertently lower the perceived threat, causing patients to reject effortful recovery.

The Trajectory: Awakening into Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Good. Verified clinical efficacy overcomes behavioral friction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Stents only open arteries; they do not cure the underlying disease.

The Unavoidable Lie: Believing that a quick, painless procedure means you are permanently out of danger.

Alethekanon:
The data exposes a systemic optimization failure. We have perfected the acute clinical intervention but neglected the behavioral transition. True efficiency requires closing the post-discharge information gap.

Awwthekanon:
It is so scary to face our own mortality. When doctors make the procedure feel small, it's natural to want to believe we are fine. Patients need gentle, continuous emotional support to heal both body and mind.

Brothekanon:
Bro, getting a stent put in your wrist and thinking you're ironman is peak human denial. Don't skip the gym just because the doctor did a magic trick on your artery. Go do your rehab!
